Definition: the 22nd, 14th and an obsolete letter (G4742 as a cross) of the Greek alphabet (intermediate between the 5th and 6th), used as numbers; denoting respectively 600, 60 and 6; 666 as a numeral:--six hundred threescore and six.
BiblicalUsage: These three letters are the old way of writing six hundred threescore and six, the number of the beast. The Greek text behind the audit spells the number out in words, while other ancient copies write it as three letters, chi, xi, and stigma. The letters stand for a number, and the number stands for a man.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the number matters less than what it points to: a human system that demands worship, and a God who has already numbered its days.
